First Regular Bail Application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (hereinafter referred to as 'B.N.S.S.') and Section 439 of CrPC, has been filed on behalf of the Petitioner, Kasim for grant of Regular Bail in FIR No. 1525/2015 under Section 498A/306/304B/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC'), as well as, the Supplementary Charge-Sheet under Section 174(A) of IPC, registered at Police Station Seemapuri, Delhi.
2.
It is submitted that his Bail Application has been dismissed by the learned Trial Court vide Order dated 06.03.2025.
The Charge-Sheet in this Case was filed on 27.01.2016.
The matter is pending trial before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate for Prosecution evidence.
Out of 20 witnesses, 15 material and formal witnesses have been recorded.
Nothing incriminating hence come in the testimony of these witnesses.
Only formal witnesses remained to be examined and there is no likelihood of the Applicant This is a digitally signed order.

3. The Regular Bail was granted to the Applicant on 18.12.2017.
He had appeared before the learned Trial Court regularly.
On 18.01.2024, learned counsel for the Applicant could not appear and the matter got adjourned.

On 20.04.2024, the Applicant was not feeling well but his counsel appeared on his behalf and apprised the Court of this ill-health, despite which NBWs were issued against him and the surety bond was forfeited.

sentences.text: The Applicant was having financial difficulties and was unable to pay his counsel's fee and was unable to contact his counsel to find out the date in the learned Trial Court.
He has never received any warrants/summons of the Court.
After recovering from his illness, he travelled to UP in search of job.
The Applicant was unaware of the proceedings initiated under Section 82 Cr.P.C.
He was not residing at his residence at the time when the NBWs were executed against him.
He has been declared an offender vide Order dated 24.07.2024.
He was arrested on 30.07.2024 under Section 174(A) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and since then, he is in judicial custody.
5. The Bail is sought on the grounds that the investigations and the trial have been completed and the Supplementary Charge-Sheet under Section 174(A) IPC has been filed.
All material witnesses have been examined.
He belongs to humble law abiding family with limited means of income.
Before issuing the Proclamation, learned Trial Court ought to have given the reasons for its belief that the Applicant is absconding.
The proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. was never served upon him.
6. The Applicant is a permanent resident at the address furnished on the judicial record.
He was young when the alleged incident happened and was arrested.
He has the responsibility to maintain his family members on his This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/09/2025 at 23:10:43 shoulder.
Hence, a prayer is made that he may be granted Bail.

7. Learned Prosecutor for the State, submits that the learned Trial Court while issuing the Proclamation against the Applicant, had noted his conduct who has been protracting the trial on one pretext or the other.
Furthermore, the trial is at the fag end as 15 out of 18 Prosecution witnesses have already been recorded.
Considering his conduct, there is everylikelihood that he may abscond against thereby delaying the trial.
Hence, the Bail Application is opposed.

Submissions heard and record perused.
8.
The Applicant has been on Bail since 2018 in the present Case and had been appearing regularly.
However, he failed to appear on one date i.e. 20.04.2024 when warrants were issued.

Thereafter,
Proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., was directed to be executed.
The Applicant was declared an offender vide Order dated 24.07.2024.
Practically, he was not present for about three months during which the Applicant has been declared an offender.

9. Considering the aforesaid circumstances that he has been regularly facing the trial and most of the witnesses have already been recorded, no fruitful purpose would be served in keeping him in Jail, essentially for the offence under Section 174(A) IPC.

In the circumstances, the Applicant is granted Regular Bail, on the following terms and conditions:
a) The Petitioner/accused shall furnish a personal bond of Rs.25,000/- and one surety of the like amount, subject to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court.
